description: Developing Outreach for Heat Resilience in North Carolina’s Sandhills Region is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by North Carolina DHHS, Climate and Health Program. Many North Carolinians are at increasing risk of heat-related illness. The Climate and Health team in the state's Department of Health and Human Services focused on the Sandhills Region of the state to develop culturally responsive outreach strategies that can enhance residents' resilience to extreme heat. Coverage: North Carolina (2024). The toolkit gives North Carolina as the location, 2024 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.

outcomes: Department personnel conducted interviews with partners in Bladen, Robeson, Sampson, and Scotland counties to understand their experience and heat safety programming needs. The interviews confirmed what the team was seeing in the data: outdoor workers, people living in poverty, older adults, and young children were at a higher risk of heat-related illness. In addition, the team saw that lack of transportation and air conditioning were significant factors that limited communities’ ability to adapt to extreme heat events. This lack also affects many migrant farmworkers, who are regularly exposed to high heat.
